# fondaco_quarantine (Resource)

A blocked coordinate: the registry refuses to serve it with 409 while this exists, at this site and at every site the block replicates to.

A block removes access, never bytes. Destroying the resource releases the block and the coordinate is served again — which is why an incident response can be expressed as code and reverted the same way.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Block a version while an advisory is investigated. The bytes stay where
# they are; only access is removed, at this site and every site the block
# replicates to. Deleting this resource releases it.
resource "fondaco_quarantine" "cve_2026_0001" {
  feed       = "releases"
  coordinate = "maven:com.example:widget@1.4.2"
  detail     = "CVE-2026-0001, waiting on 1.4.3"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `coordinate` (String) Canonical coordinate, e.g. `maven:com.example:lib@1.0.0` or `npm:left-pad@1.3.0`.
- `feed` (String) Feed the coordinate belongs to.

### Optional

- `detail` (String) Free text kept in the audit log — a CVE identifier, a ticket, whatever the next person will need.
- `reason` (String) Why it is blocked. Defaults to `manual`. `cross_site_conflict` is refused: that block is derived from a recorded conflict and is cleared by resolving the conflict.

### Read-Only

- `created_at` (String) When the block was recorded.
- `id` (String) `<feed>/<coordinate>/<reason>`.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# Blocks are imported as <feed>/<coordinate>[/<reason>]; the reason defaults
# to "manual".
terraform import fondaco_quarantine.cve 'releases/maven:com.example:widget@1.4.2/manual'
```
